item.description:
[Episode 21] The Secret Club in the White House... War of the Gods ([21화] 백악관의 비밀 클럽… 신들의 전쟁)

☞ View from Episode 1 (☞ 1화부터 보기)

☞ Character Introduction (☞ 등장인물 소개)

At the same time, in the east wing of the White House in Washington D.C., three men faced each other in a triangular formation. (같은 시각, 워싱턴 D.C. 백악관 동쪽에선 세 남자가 삼각형 구도로 서로를 바라봤다.)

At the head of the table sat Alistair Carrington, the chairman of Dudalel and a titan representing old money. On his left was Patrick MacWilliams, vice president of Dudalel Tech. At the far end sat Marcus Calhoun, the Deputy Under Secretary of Policy at the U.S. State Department. (상석엔 듀다엘의 의장이자 올드 머니를 대변하는 거물 앨리스터 캐링턴, 왼쪽엔 듀다엘 테크의 패트릭 맥윌리엄스 부사장, 그리고 말석엔 미 국무부 정책차관 마커스 칼훈이 앉았다.)

The three gathered every six months at a private club near the White House. Their room, which could only be reached by passing through the buzz of the main hall and reaching the end of the corridor, was known to exist by only a select few. When a waiter opened the door to take their orders, a red leather sofa, dark walnut paneling, and the low-hanging glow of a chandelier came into full view. (셋은 반년에 한 번씩 백악관 근처 프라이빗 클럽에 모였다. 메인 홀의 웅성거림을 지나 복도 끝에 이르러서야 나타나는 이들의 방은 극소수만이 존재를 알고 있다. 웨이터가 주문을 받으려 방문을 열자, 붉은 가죽 소파, 짙은 월넛 패널, 낮게 깔린 샹들리에 조명이 한눈에 들어왔다.)

To put it somewhat dramatically, one could say the atmosphere was where Washington's raw power breathed. It was a secret place that had witnessed the whispered conversations of countless politicians since its founding in the 19th century. (과장을 좀 보태면, 워싱턴 권력이 날것의 상태로 숨 쉬는 분위기라 말할 수 있겠다. 19세기에 문을 연 이래 수많은 정객의 밀담을 지켜온 비밀스러운 장소였다.)

As the waiter stood upright to take the order, Marcus recited the evening menu that would be laid on the table, as if an actor performing a role. (웨이터가 반듯한 자세로 주문을 받자, 마커스는 배우가 연기를 하는 것처럼 테이블에 놓일 저녁 메뉴를 읊었다.)

"Crab cake, filet mignon cooked rare, wild mushroom bisque with truffle." (“크랩 케이크, 레어로 익힌 안심 스테이크, 트러플을 곁들인 야생 버섯 비스크.”)

No one even glanced at the menu. After all, this was not a gathering where gastronomy was the priority. (누구도 메뉴판에 눈길조차 주지 않았다. 어차피 식도락이 중요한 모임은 아니기 때문이다.)

As the waiter left the room, Marcus poured the pre-decanted 1961 Château Cheval Blanc into the glasses. (마커스는 웨이터가 방을 나서자 미리 디캔팅해둔 샤토 슈발 블랑 1961을 잔에 따랐다.)

"This wine isn't drunk to celebrate a good day. The day you drink this *becomes* a good day." (“이 와인은 좋은 날을 기념하기 위해 마시는 게 아닙니다. 이걸 마시는 날이 바로 좋은 날이 되는 거죠.”)

Patrick raised his glass. (패트릭이 잔을 들었다.)

"I agree. In that case, we should add news that will make today even more memorable. A report has arrived from South Korea." (“동감입니다. 그렇다면 오늘을 그 이상으로 기억하게 만들 소식을 덧붙여야겠군요. 한국에서 보고가 도착했습니다.”)

Patrick took a sip of wine and then began to lay out the technological landscape. He briefed them fluently without any rehearsal. (패트릭은 와인을 한 모금 머금더니, 기술 지형을 펼쳐 보이기 시작했다. 리허설 없이도 유창하게 브리핑을 하는 모습이었다.)

"Sariel is about to begin full-scale operation. Sariel is more than just a surveillance system. It will integrate not only South Korean military reconnaissance aircraft but also American spy satellite constellations and signals intelligence, allowing it to thoroughly and in real-time analyze all information around the Korean Peninsula." (“사리엘이 곧 전면 가동에 들어갑니다. 사리엘은 단순한 감시 시스템이 아닙니다. 한국군의 정찰기뿐 아니라 미 첩보 위성군과 신호정보까지 통합해 한반도 주변 정보를 샅샅이, 그리고 실시간으로 분석할 수 있게 됩니다.)

Patrick's voice lowered. (패트릭의 목소리가 낮아졌다.)

"It's not on the level of simple wiretapping. Radar signals are the basics; it even intercepts FISINT—the machine-language command signals exchanged between North Korean electronic equipment—in real time. If North Korea presses a missile button, it will grasp what command code is entered into the launcher without even a 0.1-second delay." (“단순 도청 수준이 아닙니다. 레이더 신호는 기본이고, 북한군 전자 장비 간에 오가는 기계어 명령 신호인 FISINT까지 실시간으로 가로챕니다. 북한이 미사일 버튼을 누르면, 발사대에 어떤 명령 코드를 입력하는지 0.1초의 시차도 없이 파악합니다.”)

Alistair and Marcus listened to Patrick's words, quietly taking a sip of their wine. (앨리스터와 마커스는 패트릭의 말을 들으며 조용히 와인을 한 모금 들이켰다.)

"War is no longer conducted by people." (“전쟁은 더 이상 사람이 수행하지 않습니다.”)

Alistair set down his glass. (앨리스터가 잔을 내려놓았다.)

Despite outwardly having the scholarly appearance of an Ivy League political science professor, he was a corporate executive faithful to his main role as a ruthless capitalist. The waiter naturally placed an oyster dish next to the untouched caviar in front of Alistair. Alistair was the type who wouldn't touch his food until the main discussion was over. (언뜻 보면 아이비리그 정치학 교수 느낌의 학자풍 외모를 풍기면서도, 본업은 냉혹한 자본가의 역할에 충실한 기업 중역이었다. 웨이터는 손대지 않은 캐비아 옆에 굴 요리를 앨리스터 앞에 자연스레 놓았다. 앨리스터는 본론이 끝나기 전까지는 음식에 손을 대지 않는 사람이었다.)

"So, Patrick, what do all those fancy technical descriptions mean for us?" (“그래서 패트릭, 그 화려한 기술적 수사들이 우리한테는 어떤 의미인가?”)

Alistair asked, fidgeting with his napkin. (앨리스터가 냅킨을 만지작거리며 물었다.)

"What we want isn't a surveillance camera. It's the order that data will create." (“우리가 원하는 건 감시 카메라가 아니야. 그 데이터가 만들어낼 질서지.”)

Patrick replied. (패트릭이 답했다.)

"Externally, to the South Korean people, it will be promoted as a shield to deter war in East Asia. But that justification will become the perfect weapon for us to eliminate uncontrollable variables." (“대외적으로는, 한국인들에게는 동아시아에서 전쟁을 억제할 방패로 선전될 겁니다. 하지만 그 명분이 우리에겐 통제 불능의 변수를 제거하는 가장 완벽한 무기가 되겠죠.”)

At that, Alistair toyed with the stem of his wine glass. (그러자 앨리스터가 와인잔의 스템을 만지작거렸다.)

"You know, among the countless diplomats in history, I respect Metternich the most." (“나는 역사상 수많은 외교관 중 메테르니히를 가장 존경하네.”)

Alistair's eyes sharpened. Then his characteristic scholarly tone, reserved only for private settings for a long time, emerged. (앨리스터의 눈빛이 날카로워졌다. 그러더니, 오랜 기간 비공개 석상에서만 꺼내는 특유의 학자 말투가 나왔다.)

"Metternich realized after Napoleon: you don't need to win every war. You just need to hold the balance. America never managed either. It bled money and blood into irrelevant wars while neglecting the rest of the board. A power vacuum was created, and various unruly factions began to act up." (“메테르니히는 나폴레옹 이후에 깨달았지. 모든 전쟁을 이길 필요는 없다. 균형을 쥐고 있으면 된다. 미국은 어느 쪽도 하지 못했어. 상관없는 전쟁에 피와 돈을 쏟아부으면서 나머지 판은 방치했지. 힘의 진공이 생겨났고, 잡스러운 세력들이 설치기 시작했어.”)

It sounded like a pretentious political science lecture, yet the other two listened as intently as freshmen. (젠체하는 정치학 강의처럼 들렸지만, 나머지 둘은 신입생 마냥 귀를 기울였다.)

"We need to restore balance. *Our* balance. The way to maintain that balance is not through speeches or treaties. It's technological superiority—pulling so far ahead that the other side can't even think to close the gap. Sariel is that gap. Order doesn't come from appeal; it comes from fear." (“우리는 다시 균형을 잡아야 해. 우리의 균형을. 그 균형을 유지하는 방법은 연설이나 조약이 아니야. 상대편이 격차를 줄일 생각조차 못 할 만큼 벌려놓는 기술적 우위지. 사리엘이 그 격차야. 질서는 호소가 아니라 공포에서 나오니까.”)

Only after finishing his speech did Alistair finally pick up the oyster. (앨리스터는 말을 마치고 나서야 비로소 굴을 집어 들었다.)

He tilted the shell with caviar and swallowed it in one bite. It was the signal to begin the meal. (캐비아를 올린 껍데기를 기울여 한 입에 삼켰다. 식사를 시작하자는 신호였다.)

Patrick gave a cold smile. (패트릭이 차갑게 미소 지었다.)

"When China and North Korea realize the true nature of Sariel and start flailing, and when they know there's nothing they can do—Alistair, you'll see that you've moved one step closer to your goal." (“중국과 북한이 사리엘의 실체를 깨닫고 발작할 때, 그리고 아무것도 할 수 없음을 알게 될 때—앨리스터, 당신의 목표에 한 발 더 나아갔음을 보게 될 겁니다.")

As the meal drew to a close, Marcus tried to lighten the mood with an Alistair-style joke. (식사가 끝나갈 무렵, 마커스가 분위기를 환기하려 앨리스터식 농담을 던졌다.)

"Let's stop the heavy talk for now. How about we finish tonight with key lime pie instead of Sacher torte? It seems like we need a light, American finish after Metternich's heavy philosophy." (“무거운 얘기는 여기까지 하죠. 오늘은 자허토르테 대신 키 라임 파이로 마무리하는 게 어떻겠습니까. 메테르니히의 무거운 철학 뒤엔 미국식의 가벼운 끝맛이 필요할 것 같군요.”)

item.title: Shut Up and Woo Honam: A Strategy for Party Leadership or Regime Security? (닥치고 호남 구애 작전… 당권 넘어 정권 안위용인가)
item.description:
Shut Up and Woo Honam: A Strategy for Party Leadership or Regime Security? (닥치고 호남 구애 작전… 당권 넘어 정권 안위용인가)

President Lee Jae-myung has been sending strong courtship messages to the Honam region daily, leveraging astronomical-scale semiconductor investments. He has even cited the phrase attributed to Admiral Yi Sun-shin, "If there is no Honam, there is no nation," expressing special affection for the region. (이재명 대통령이 천문학적 규모의 호남 반도체 투자를 앞세워 연일 호남에 강한 구애 메시지를 보내고 있습니다. 이순신 장군의 말로 알려진 “약무호남 시무국가”, 즉 “호남이 없으면 나라가 없다”는 표현까지 인용하며 호남에 대한 각별한 애정을 드러내고 있습니다.)

On the 30th of last month, President Lee personally attended the "Southwestern Region Advanced Industrial Development Vision National Report" held in Gwangju. At the event, regarding the 800 trillion won semiconductor investments by Samsung Electronics and SK Hynix, he stated, "I view this as a historical and national compensation to Honam, which endured discrimination, pain, and resentment to build and protect the democracy of the Republic of Korea, and I will ensure it succeeds without any setbacks." He also added, "I am truly delighted to be able to rectify, even slightly, the discrimination between the Yeongnam and Honam regions." <<> Until now, President Lee and his administration had emphasized that this large-scale semiconductor investment was a corporate decision based on economic feasibility studies. However, by mentioning "historical compensation" and "rectifying regional discrimination," President Lee has given the impression that this investment is intertwined not only with pure corporate judgment but also with political and regional balance considerations. This means the economic logic touted by the government and the political symbolism emphasized by the president have been placed side by side in a single scene. <<> Just the day before, at the "Three Major Mega Projects National Report" held at the presidential office, such political background was scarcely revealed. It seemed there was caution about the potential perception of political pressure on corporations. However, in Gwangju, it was different. President Lee put forward the significance of consideration and compensation for Honam. This is why political circles interpret the announcement of this semiconductor investment as a political gamble targeting public sentiment in Honam, going beyond mere industrial policy. <<> The People Power Party is criticizing that President Lee has unfairly discriminated against other regions to win over Honam voters and placed undue burdens on corporations. In contrast, ruling party circles evaluate it as a national investment for Honam's development and a measure to rectify long-standing regional imbalances. Regarding the same issue, the opposition sees it as "favoritism toward Honam," while the ruling camp views it as "balanced development." <<> Within the ruling party, there are interpretations that this investment is not unrelated to the dynamics of the August party convention. There are observations that it is a card for the leadership race to check former Representative Chung Cheong-rae and boost pro-Lee candidates like Representatives Kim Min-seok and Song Young-gil. Honam remains a region with decisive influence in the Democratic Party's leadership competition. Its membership ratio and voter turnout are high, and its symbolic weight is significant. It is highly likely that a candidate gaining an advantage in Honam will also secure a favorable position in the leadership race. <<> In fact, in the Gwangju and South Jeolla regions, there is a strong welcoming atmosphere toward this semiconductor investment announcement. It is reported that support for President Lee is clearly on the rise in the Honam region. This trend could lead to increased support for pro-Lee candidates vying for party leadership. Some assessments suggest President Lee's gamble to check former Representative Chung Cheong-rae and boost Representatives Kim Min-seok and Song Young-gil is proving effective so far. <<> However, it is difficult to view this semiconductor investment solely as a card for the party convention. Recently, approval ratings for President Lee and the Democratic Party have been on a continuous decline. Warnings for the Lee Jae-myung administration have intensified due to overlapping factors such as public criticism over reckless attempts by the ruling camp to dismiss charges in President Lee's case, public sentiment turning away due to defeats in key battlegrounds of the June 3 election, and divisions within the ruling camp's support base caused by conflicts between pro-Chung and pro-Lee factions. <<> If left unchecked, this could escalate into a governance crisis. Past administrations have often faced decline when their core support base wavered. Notably, when Honam, the last bastion, turned its back, progressive governments inevitably faced crises. The Roh Moo-hyun administration is a prime example. In the late stages of the Roh administration, state approval ratings in Honam fell to the low 20% range, ultimately leading to the failure to extend the regime and the collapse of the pro-Roh faction. <<> President Lee appears to judge that now is a watershed moment to prevent such a crisis. Thus, he has brought out an unprecedented investment card of astronomical scale aimed at Honam, his core support base. This is why this semiconductor investment is interpreted not merely as a tool for leadership struggles but as a card for long-term regime security. <<> The Lee Jae-myung administration needs to maintain high approval ratings in Honam to operate state affairs stably. Furthermore, analyses suggest that issues of great concern to President Lee, such as the dismissal of charges in various trials and post-retirement safety, are not unrelated to his political support base. For President Lee, ensuring this semiconductor investment does not fail or go awry has become the top priority in state affairs. <<> At the Gwangju national report on the 30th of last month, President Lee repeatedly emphasized that this semiconductor investment is "historical compensation for discrimination against Honam." He stated, "There clearly was discrimination between Yeongnam and Honam," and compared the cumulative historical investment volumes, suggesting that even this investment is merely a drop in the bucket. <<> This directly refutes claims that the Honam semiconductor investment constitutes preferential treatment. The logic is that less investment has been made in Honam compared to other regions, and as a result, there is spare capacity in electricity, water, and land, making investment in Honam only natural. However, there are also criticisms that President Lee, by mentioning compensation for Honam and rectifying discrimination, has himself reinforced the impression of a politically motivated investment, especially given the government's earlier emphasis on it being a voluntary corporate decision. President Lee also stated that the corporate investment was "induced and attracted." <<> Just the day before, at the three mega-projects report at the presidential office, there was extreme caution against political controversy. But in Gwangju, it was different. Interpretations suggest the administration aimed to capture Honam public sentiment by revealing how much it cares for the region. <<> President Lee's remarks are imbued with strong affection for Honam. During the last presidential election, he borrowed Admiral Yi Sun-shin's words, saying, "If there is no Honam, there is no nation." This time, he also said, "Without Honam, there is no country." <<> Previously, President Lee has said, "Honam is not the Democratic Party's stronghold but a bamboo cane that straightens the party," and "The spirit of Gwangju created today's democracy." During the June 3 election, he criticized the controversy over Starbucks, calling it "an insult to Gwangju citizens." During the presidential election, he promised to include the spirit of the May 18 Democratization Movement in the preamble of the constitution. He vowed to make Gwangju an AI hub city and fully supported the integration of Gwangju and South Jeolla. <<> President Lee is from Andong, North Gyeongsang Province. Nevertheless, his repeated emphasis on his love for Honam is interpreted in two ways. One is a political debt to Honam, which made him president. The other is a practical necessity for governance stability and control over the party. <<> Previous Democratic Party presidents from the Yeongnam region, such as Roh Moo-hyun and Moon Jae-in, followed a similar path. They became presidents as so-called "Yeongnam candidates chosen by Honam." However, when the emotional and political alliance with Honam weakened, governance faced significant crises. Honam's support was absolute in President Lee becoming party leader and winning the presidential election. <<> In the 2017 Democratic Party presidential primary, President Lee placed third in Honam with about 19% of the vote. Former President Moon Jae-in, from Busan, secured first place with nearly 60% of the vote. Moon was elected as the presidential candidate and eventually became president. However, in the 2021 Democratic Party primary, President Lee defeated former Prime Minister Lee Nak-yeon, who is from Honam, in the Honam region. That victory served as a decisive stepping stone to becoming the presidential candidate. In last year's presidential election, President Lee received overwhelming support from Honam in both the primary and the general election, leading to his presidency. <<> But recently, the controversy over dismissing charges, the results of the June 3 election, and leadership conflicts have caused President Lee's approval ratings to decline steadily. The Honam region's approval ratings are no exception. Warning signs of a crisis have been triggered for the Lee Jae-myung administration. The courtship of Honam and the astronomical semiconductor investment can be seen as emerging from this political backdrop. <<> Regarding this semiconductor investment, the Yeongnam, Chungcheong, and Seoul metropolitan areas have voiced criticism, saying it only favors Honam. There is discontent that some regions with locational conditions no less favorable than Honam are wondering why Honam alone receives such massive preferential treatment. Such public opinion could become a burden on national approval ratings. <<> Nevertheless, President Lee is highly likely to continue his courtship of Honam for the time being. In politics, the core support base is a foundation that must not be shaken. Amid a situation where the core support base is wavering due to election results and leadership conflicts, it appears he has judged that solidifying Honam first is the top priority. Especially in the leadership race against former Representative Chung Cheong-rae, securing public sentiment in Honam is crucial for pro-Lee candidates to gain strength. <<> Following his visit to Gwangju on the 30th, President Lee plans to visit Asan and Jinju sequentially this month. This is interpreted as a strategy to secure Honam first with semiconductors, then attend to Chungcheong and Yeongnam. It suggests that even if "Honam favoritism" arguments arise outside Honam, he will prioritize consolidating the core support base. <<> How President Lee's moves will affect the leadership race is also a point of interest. It is said that support for President Lee in Honam is clearly rising. Synthesizing recent accounts from each candidate's camp, analyses suggest that the approval ratings of pro-Lee Representatives Kim Min-seok and Song Young-gil are on the rise, while former Representative Chung Cheong-rae is in a stagnant phase. <<> Of course, Chung's camp claims that support is solid in non-Honam regions. However, given the high proportion of party members and voter turnout in Honam, it is difficult to deny that a candidate gaining an edge in Honam has an advantage in the leadership race. There are assessments that President Lee's semiconductor gamble has been effective, at least so far. <<> Based on these shifts in sentiment within the ruling camp, President Lee is attempting to reunite the dispersed support base. This is because stable governance is possible only when Honam consolidates and supports him. If so, he likely expects that national approval ratings, which turned downward around the June 3 election, could rebound. <<> If national approval ratings recover, the issue of dismissing charges—considered President Lee's top concern—could gain momentum again. This is interpreted as being directly linked to President Lee's post-retirement safety and security. For President Lee, this semiconductor investment is a core state task that absolutely must not fail. Analyses suggest that the scene where he bowed his head deeply to express gratitude to Samsung Electronics Chairman Lee Jae-yong and SK Chairman Chey Tae-won reflects this sense of urgency. <<> The Honam semiconductor investment is no longer a simple regional development project. It has become both an industrial policy and a regional political strategy for the Lee Jae-myung administration, and a gamble intertwined with the internal power dynamics of the ruling camp. There is one key question. Can this investment translate into actual factories, jobs, and an industrial ecosystem? Honam's public sentiment cannot be captured forever by an announcement alone. Only when promises turn into construction sites, construction sites into jobs, and jobs into the region's future can a political gamble become a successful policy. (이 대통령은 지난달 30일 광주에서 열린 ‘서남권 첨단산업 발전 비전 국민 보고회’에 직접 참석했습니다. 이 자리에서 삼성전자와 SK하이닉스의 800조원대 반도체 투자에 대해 “차별의 고통과 설움을 견뎌내며 대한민국의 민주주의를 만들고 지켜온 호남에 대한 역사적·국민적 보상으로 생각하고, 일체의 차질 없이 반드시 성공시키겠다”고 했습니다. 또 “영·호남 지역 차별을 조금이라도 교정할 수 있게 돼 참으로 기쁘다”고도 했습니다.)

item.title: Lee: "Expand the Base," Moon: "Internal Unity"... A Two-Hour Meeting with Different Goals (文 “내부 단합” 李 “외연 확장”… 결 달랐던 2시간 만남)
item.description:
Lee: "Expand the Base," Moon: "Internal Unity"... A Two-Hour Meeting with Different Goals (文 “내부 단합” 李 “외연 확장”… 결 달랐던 2시간 만남)

President Lee Jae-myung and former President Moon Jae-in met at the Blue House on the 1st for lunch together. Both emphasized "national unity," but there were subtle differences in how they interpreted the term. Former President Moon stressed that "internal party unity" should come first, while President Lee focused on the need to create a "structural majority through expanding the base." Although President Lee did not provide a detailed explanation of "structural majority," it was interpreted as meaning the need to embrace not only the Democratic Party's support base but also centrist voters. With internal conflicts between the pro-Lee and pro-Moon factions intensifying ahead of the Democratic Party's August leadership election, the two proposed different approaches to unity. The two also reportedly discussed the relationship between the party and the administration. (이재명 대통령과 문재인 전 대통령이 1일 청와대에서 만나 오찬을 함께했다. 두 사람은 ‘국민 통합’을 강조했지만, 그 의미에 대해서는 미묘한 온도차를 보였다. 문 전 대통령은 “당내 통합”을 우선해야 한다고 말한 반면, 이 대통령은 “외연 확장을 통한 구조적 다수”를 만들어야 한다는 데 방점을 뒀다. ‘구조적 다수’에 대해 이 대통령이 구체적인 설명을 하진 않았으나, 민주당 지지층뿐만 아니라 중도층까지 끌어안아야 한다는 뜻으로 해석됐다. 더불어민주당 8월 당대표 선거를 앞두고 친명·친청 갈등이 격화하는 상황에서 통합에 대해 서로 결이 다른 해결책을 제시한 것이다. 두 사람은 당정 관계에 대한 이야기도 나눈 것으로 알려졌다.)

President Lee and former President Moon met at the Blue House's Sangchunjae pavilion for about two hours, sharing a lunch and a walk. The pair embraced upon meeting, asking about each other's health and well-being in a warm atmosphere. The lunch menu featured bibimbap and assorted rice cakes, symbolizing integration and harmony. Former President Moon said, "To move toward national unity, I believe internal party cohesion is the starting point. Only when the Democratic Party unites first, and then achieves greater unity with the democratic reform camp and those who participated in the 'revolution of light' on that foundation, can we gather the people's hearts as one." This appeared to mean that internal Democratic Party unity should be followed by solidarity with the broader pro-government camp, including the Fatherland Innovation Party. Former President Moon added, "I hope you exercise greater leadership and surely realize the dream of becoming a president for all." (이 대통령과 문 전 대통령은 이날 청와대 상춘재에서 만나 약 2시간 동안 오찬과 산책을 했다. 두 사람은 만나자마자 포옹을 했고, 서로의 건강과 안부를 묻는 등 화기애애한 모습을 보였다. 오찬 메뉴로는 통합과 화합의 의미를 담은 비빔밥과 모둠떡이 준비됐다. 문 전 대통령은 “국민통합으로 나아가려면 역시 당내의 단합, 이게 출발점이라고 생각한다”며 “민주당이 먼저 단합하고, 그 위에서 민주개혁 진영 그리고 빛의 혁명을 함께했던 세력들과의 더 큰 단합을 이루어내야 국민의 마음을 하나로 모을 수 있다”고 했다. 민주당 내부 통합에 이어 조국혁신당을 비롯한 범여권과의 연대가 필요하다는 취지로 보인다. 문 전 대통령은 “더 큰 리더십을 발휘하셔서 모두의 대통령이라는 꿈을 반드시 이루시기를 바란다”고 했다.)

In response, President Lee said, "Internal unity is also very important—the core must be solid," but added, "We must continuously expand the base and strive to create a 'structural majority,' and we need to produce results from that to back it up; it can't just be words." Regarding the meaning of "structural majority," a Blue House official explained, "It means securing a stable majority support base by broadening support to include center-right voters, excluding the extremes." (이에 이 대통령은 “내부의 단합도 매우 중요하다, 속이 단단해야 되겠다”라면서도 “끊임없이 외연을 확장하고, ‘구조적 다수’를 만들기 위해서 노력해야 되고, 거기서 끊임없이 성과를 내야 뒷받침되는 거지, 말로만은 안 되지 않느냐”고 했다. ‘구조적 다수’의 의미에 대해 청와대 관계자는 “양극단을 제외하고 중도 우파까지 지지 기반을 넓혀 안정적인 다수 지지층을 확보해야 한다는 뜻”이라고 했다.)

Analysts suggest that the simultaneous unity messages from the two men stemmed from the uncontrollable rise of divisions within the ruling camp. Recently, the old mainstream of the Democratic Party, including the pro-Moon faction, has criticized President Lee for appointing figures from the opposition or former prosecutors and showing signs of backtracking on prosecutorial reform. In response, "New Lee Jae-myung" supporters have pushed back, calling it an "attempt to kill Lee Jae-myung," leading to a power struggle between the new and old mainstreams. Blue House Senior Secretary for Political Affairs Hong Ik-pyo stated that the two agreed "neither side benefits from hurting others with derogatory terms." (두 사람이 동시에 통합 메시지를 낸 것은 여권 내 분열이 걷잡을 수 없이 커졌기 때문이라는 분석이다. 최근 친청계를 비롯한 민주당 구주류는 이 대통령이 야권 또는 검찰 출신 인사를 등용하고, 검찰 개혁도 후퇴하는 기미가 보인다며 비판하고 있다. 반면 이 대통령을 지지하는 ‘뉴이재명’은 이를 “이재명 죽이기”라고 반발하면서 신·구주류간 세력 대결로 번지는 양상이다. 두 사람은 “멸칭 등으로 상처 입히는 것은 어느 누구에게도 도움이 되지 않는다”는 데 뜻을 모았다고 홍익표 청와대 정무수석은 밝혔다.)

Former President Moon said, "Regarding inter-Korean relations, there has been no response from the North yet. However, I believe that if we continue knocking on the door for dialogue and manage the situation stably, an opportunity for renewed talks will eventually arise." This was interpreted as a request for additional government efforts to facilitate inter-Korean dialogue. In response, President Lee said, "It seems the military pressure on the North for the military coup and the praetorian coup was truly excessive." He was referring to the deterioration of relations due to incidents such as the North Korean drone incursion during the Yoon Suk-yeol administration, which has made inter-Korean dialogue difficult. He reportedly sought advice from former President Moon on resolving inter-Korean issues. (문 전 대통령은 “남북관계에 있어서는 북측에서 아직까지 호응이 없다”며 “그러나 계속해서 대화의 문을 두드리고, 상황을 안정적으로 관리해 나간다면 언젠가는 다시 대화할 수 있는 계기가 마련되리라고 믿는다”고 했다. 남북 대화 성사를 위한 정부의 추가적인 노력을 당부한 것으로 해석됐다. 이에 대해 이 대통령은 “군사쿠데타, 친위쿠데타를 위해 북쪽을 군사적으로 압박한 게 정말 너무 컸던 것 같다”고 했다. 윤석열 정부 때 발생한 북한 무인기 사태 등으로 관계가 악화돼 남북 대화가 어려운 상황이라는 것이다. 그러면서 문 전 대통령에게 남북관계를 풀기 위한 조언을 청했다고 한다.)

Regarding the government's announcement of a semiconductor cluster in the southwestern region, former President Moon said, "Seeing the Gwangju event made me really happy. In fact, during our administration, we did a lot in that southwestern sea area with renewable energy, wind power, and solar power." President Lee responded, "It became possible because of what was done a lot (during the Moon Jae-in administration)." (문 전 대통령은 정부의 서남권 반도체 클러스터 조성 발표에 대해서는 “광주 행사 보고 정말 기분이 좋았다. 사실 우리 정부 때 서남해 그 지역에 신재생에너지, 풍력, 태양광발전을 많이 (했다)”고 했다. 이에 이 대통령은 “(문재인 정부에서) 많이 해 놓은 것 때문에 가능해진 것”이라고 화답했다.)

The official meeting between the two took place about a year after President Lee's inauguration. After lunch, they reportedly walked and talked from Sangchunjae to the main building. After the meeting, former President Moon met with Democratic Party lawmaker Yoon Kun-young and shared his thoughts, saying, "It was a satisfactory meeting. Heading back to Pyeongsan now, I feel much more at ease than when I came up to Seoul." However, a pro-Moon figure within the Democratic Party commented, "That implies he came up with a heavy heart. Even just reading between the lines of his public remarks, it seems the meeting wasn't entirely amicable." (두 사람의 공식 회동은 이 대통령 취임 1년 여만에 성사됐다. 두 사람은 오찬을 마친 뒤 상춘재에서 본관까지 걸어가며 대화를 나눴다고 한다. 문 전 대통령은 회동이 끝난 뒤 민주당 윤건영 의원과 만나 “만족스러운 회동이었다. 서울에 올라올 때보다 평산으로 내려가는 지금 한결 마음이 놓인다”는 소회를 밝혔다고 한다. 그러나 민주당의 한 친문계 인사는 “무거운 마음을 갖고 올라왔다는 얘기고, 공개 발언의 행간만 보더라도 꼭 아름답지만은 않은 만남이었던 것 같다”고 했다.)

item.title: Kim Min-seok: "Is There a Need to Serve as Party Leader Twice?" – Jeong Cheong-rae's Side: "Is There a Need to Serve as Party Leader After Being Prime Minister?" (김민석 “당 대표를 두번 할 필요 있나” 정청래 측 “총리하다 당대표 할 필요 있나”)
item.description:
Kim Min-seok: "Is There a Need to Serve as Party Leader Twice?" – Jeong Cheong-rae's Side: "Is There a Need to Serve as Party Leader After Being Prime Minister?" (김민석 “당 대표를 두번 할 필요 있나” 정청래 측 “총리하다 당대표 할 필요 있나”)

As former Prime Minister Kim Min-seok returned to the Democratic Party on the 1st after resigning from his post and effectively announced his candidacy for the party leadership election, tensions among leadership contenders are intensifying. Former Prime Minister Kim, targeting former leader Jeong Cheong-rae who is seeking a second term, said, "It's hard to see the need to serve as party leader twice in the same way as before." In response, Jeong's side retorted, "Is there a need to serve as party leader after having been prime minister?" (김민석 전 국무총리가 1일 총리직 사퇴 후 민주당으로 돌아와 사실상 당대표 선거 출마를 공식화하면서, 당권주자 간 신경전이 고조되고 있다. 김 전 총리는 연임 도전에 나선 정청래 전 대표를 겨냥해 “지금까지 했던 방식으로 굳이 당대표를 두번이나 할 필요를 발견하기 어렵다”고 했고, 정 전 대표 측은 “총리를 하다 굳이 당대표를 할 필요는 있느냐”고 맞받았다.)

In an interview with OhmyNews, former Prime Minister Kim stated, "This is a time when we need leadership with a different color, capability, style, and strengths compared to former leader Jeong." Regarding the results of the June 3 local elections, he added, "It's dragging down (the party's approval ratings)," and stressed, "It's time for the party to move more vigorously." In a media interview later that evening, when asked about the theory of responsibility among some pro-Jeong lawmakers for the 'Candidate Unification Council (CUC) incident'—where they switched to supporting candidate Chung Mong-joon during the 2002 presidential election—Kim responded, "I have offered many apologies for my shortcomings in the past, and I intend to do so in the future as well." <<> Former Prime Minister Kim and former leader Jeong also clashed over the issue of merging with the Fatherland Innovation Party. Before the local elections, former leader Jeong had pushed for the merger but faced opposition and put it on hold. In response, Kim said, "The process of handling the merger was mishandled, leading to failure." However, in a Facebook post that day, Jeong countered, "Pan-democratic and progressive integration and solidarity are the path the Democratic Party must take for the success of the Lee Jae-myung administration, a victory in the general elections, and the re-creation of the government." <<> Former leader Jeong also visited North Jeolla Province that day. He attended the inauguration ceremony of North Jeolla Governor Lee Won-taek, a pro-Jeong figure, and also visited the city of Gunsan. A Democratic Party official noted, "Due to the nomination turmoil in the local elections, support for former leader Jeong has significantly dropped in the Honam region," adding, "The reason former leader Jeong has been frequently visiting North Jeolla recently and putting in effort is because the proportion of party members from North Jeolla is quite substantial." <<> Leadership contenders also engaged in a war of nerves over the schedule for the August 17 national convention. The regional primaries are set to be held sequentially from August 1 to 16. Former Prime Minister Kim and another leadership contender, lawmaker Song Young-gil, have raised issues over the fact that the first primary is set in the Chungcheong region, former leader Jeong's hometown, while the Honam primary, which is seen as a key decider, has been pushed back. A Democratic Party official commented, "In last year's national convention primary, it also started in Chungcheong first, with Honam, considered the highlight, later on." (김 전 총리는 오마이뉴스와의 인터뷰에서 “정 전 대표와는 다른 색깔과 역량, 다른 스타일과 장점을 가진 리더십이 필요한 때”라고 했다. 이어 6·3 지방선거 결과와 관련해 “(당 지지율을) 끌어내리는 상황”이라며 “당이 더 본격적으로 움직여야 할 때”라고 했다. 그는 이날 저녁 언론 인터뷰에선 친청계 일부 의원들이 2002년 대선 당시 정몽준 후보로 옮겨갔던 ‘후단협(후보 단일화 협의회) 사태’ 책임론을 언급하는 데 대해선 “과거에 제가 미진한 부분에 대해서는 사과드린 바도 많고 앞으로도 그럴 생각”이라고 했다.)

item.title: Accelerated Push for Military Academy Integration… Review Beginning with Current Sophomores' Admissions (사관학교 통합 속도전… 現 고2 입시부터 검토)
item.description:
Accelerated Push for Military Academy Integration… Review Beginning with Current Sophomores' Admissions (사관학교 통합 속도전… 現 고2 입시부터 검토)

As plans to merge the Army, Navy, and Air Force academies into a single "National Defense Military Academy" move forward, the Ministry of National Defense is reportedly reviewing a plan to integrate the selection of army, navy, and air force cadets as early as the 2028 academic year. According to political circles on the 1st, the Ministry of National Defense is said to have briefed some offices of lawmakers on the National Assembly's Defense Committee to this effect. This means that current high school sophomores, who will take college entrance exams next year, may need to apply to the unified National Defense Military Academy instead of the existing Army, Navy, or Air Force academies. Concerns have been raised that the information provision period for potential applicants may be insufficient. (육·해·공군 사관학교를 합쳐 ‘국군사관학교’로 만드는 통합안이 추진되고 있는 가운데, 국방부가 이르면 오는 2028학년도부터 육·해·공군 사관생도를 통합 선발하는 방안을 검토하는 것으로 전해졌다. 1일 정치권에 따르면, 국방부는 최근 국회 국방위원회 소속 일부 의원실에 이런 취지로 보고한 것으로 알려졌다. 내년에 입시를 치르는 현재 고교 2학년부터 기존 육·해·공사에 지원하는 대신 통합된 국군사관학교에 원서를 내야 할 수 있다는 뜻이다. 잠재적 응시생들을 위한 정보 제공 기간이 충분치 않을 수 있다는 우려가 제기된다.)

The Ministry of National Defense plans to announce the military academy integration plan as early as this month, followed by public hearings and legislative efforts for relevant laws. If the plan proceeds smoothly, the military is reportedly considering announcing the recruitment guidelines around April next year and admitting the first batch of integrated cadets in 2028. (국방부는 이르면 이달 중 사관학교 통합안을 발표한 뒤, 이후 공청회를 거쳐 관련 법령 입법을 추진한다는 계획이다. 군은 계획이 순조롭게 진행될 경우 내년 4월쯤 모집 요강을 공고하고, 이듬해인 2028년에 첫 통합 사관생도를 입학시키는 방안을 검토하고 있는 것으로 알려졌다.)

Indeed, the Army Academy has already posted on its website that it will announce the 2028 academic year admissions implementation plan "after government directives are issued." While admissions to military academies are regulated under separate establishment laws, under the Higher Education Act, universities must announce their admissions implementation plans 1 year and 10 months before admission to "provide applicants with admission information," yet the announcement period for military academies is inevitably much shorter. (실제로 현재 육사는 홈페이지에서 2028학년도 입학 전형 시행 계획을 “정부 지침 하달 후” 공표하겠다고 공지하고 있다. 사관학교 입학은 별도의 사관학교 설치법에 규정돼 있지만, 고등교육법상 대학들이 “응시생에게 입학에 대한 정보를 제공하기 위해” 입학 1년 10개월 전까지 입학전형 시행 계획을 공표해야 하는 데 비해 공표 기간이 훨씬 더 짧아질 수밖에 없다.)

Meanwhile, Defense Minister Ahn Kyu-baek stated at the "First Half Major Military Commanders' Meeting" held at the Ministry of National Defense that day that the integration of military academies must be achieved, saying, "If we miss this 'golden time,' the gap will become a direct loss of national interest, and furthermore, could become a matter of national survival." Regarding opposing opinions that "integration may undermine each service's expertise," he said, "That expertise must not become a 'silo.'" (이런 가운데, 안규백 국방부 장관은 이날 국방부에서 열린 ‘전반기 전군 주요 지휘관 회의’에서 사관학교 통합이 반드시 이뤄져야 한다며 “우리가 이 ‘골든 타임’을 놓치게 된다면 그 공백은 고스란히 국익의 손실이 되고, 더 나아가 국가 생존의 문제가 될 수도 있다”고 했다. ‘통합으로 각 군 전문성이 훼손될 수 있다’는 반대 여론에 대해서는 “그 전문성이 ‘칸막이’가 돼선 안 된다”고 말했다.)

However, the alumni associations of the Army, Navy, and Air Force academies are scheduled to jointly hold a "Grand Rally Against Military Academy Integration" on the 8th in front of the National Assembly in Yeouido, Seoul, with up to 1,000 participants expected. A petition posted on the National Assembly's e-petition website calling for the "halt of military academy consolidation" has garnered over 100,000 agreements as of today. (하지만 육·해·공군사관학교 총동창회는 오는 8일 서울 여의도 국회의사당 앞에서 최대 1000명가량이 참석하는 ‘사관학교 통합 반대 총궐기 대회’를 공동 개최할 예정이다. 국회 전자청원 홈페이지에 ‘사관학교 통폐합을 중단해달라’는 취지로 올라온 청원에는 이날까지 10만명 이상이 동의했다.)

item.title: Yoon Ho-Jung of the Ministry of the Interior and Safety: "Learned About Ballot Shortage Through Media Reports" (윤호중 행안 “투표지 부족, 언론 보도로 알아”)
item.description:
Yoon Ho-Jung of the Ministry of the Interior and Safety: "Learned About Ballot Shortage Through Media Reports" (윤호중 행안 “투표지 부족, 언론 보도로 알아”)

At the second agency report of the special parliamentary committee on the ballot shortage scandal held at the National Assembly on the 1st, lawmakers from the People Power Party (PPP) intensively questioned the responsibility of the Ministry of the Interior and Safety (MOIS). 'Support for public elections' is a key task of the MOIS. In response, Minister Yoon Ho-Jung replied to the effect that "if a request for support comes from the National Election Commission (NEC), we provide support tailored to that request." This implies that since the NEC made no request, they could not intervene. (1일 국회에서 열린 투표용지 부족 진상 규명을 위한 국정조사 특별위원회(국조특위) 2차 기관보고에서 국민의힘 의원들은 행정안전부 책임론을 집중 추궁했다. ‘공직선거 지원’은 행안부 주요 업무다. 이에 대해 윤호중 행안부 장관은 “선관위 지원 요청이 오면 거기에 맞는 지원을 하게 돼 있다”는 취지로 답했다. 선관위 요청이 없어 관여하지 못했다는 것이다.)

PPP lawmakers questioned Minister Yoon, who appeared as a witness that day, about when he became aware of the ballot shortage and the government's response. In response to a query from PPP lawmaker Park Soo-min (Seoul Gangnam-eul) asking, "Did you not know at all when the ballot shortage incident occurred in Songpa-gu?", Minister Yoon said, "I confirmed it after it was reported by the media." When Rep. Park pressed, "According to the Election Commission Act, the executive branch must support (election management). What is your answer?", Minister Yoon stated, "I am speaking strictly about constitutional authority." He had previously said, "The constitutional structure prevents the executive branch from directly intervening in elections." When Rep. Park asked, "The Songpa-gu Office also has a situation room. Why didn't you know?", Minister Yoon replied, "I would appreciate it if you would inquire with the Songpa-gu Office." (국민의힘 의원들은 이날 증인으로 출석한 윤 장관에게 투표용지 부족 사태 인지 시점, 정부 대응에 대해 질의했다. 윤 장관은 “송파구에서 (투표용지 부족) 사고가 났을 때 전혀 몰랐느냐”는 국민의힘 박수민(서울 강남을) 의원의 질의에 “언론에 보도된 뒤 확인됐다”고 했다. 박 의원이 “선관위법에 따라 행정부가 (선거 관리를) 지원해야 하는데, 답변이 뭐냐”고 하자, 윤 장관은 “저는 헌법적 권한에 대해 엄격하게 얘기하고 있다”고 했다. 윤 장관은 앞서 “행정부는 선거에 직접적으로 관여하지 못하도록 헌법적 구조가 돼 있다”고 했다. 박 의원이 “송파구청에도 상황실이 있는데 왜 몰랐느냐”고 묻자, 윤 장관은 “송파구청으로 문의해 주면 고맙겠다”고 했다.)

In response to a query from PPP lawmaker Kim Eun-hye (Gyeonggi Seongnam Bundang-eul) asking, "What time did you leave work on (the June 3 local election day)?", Minister Yoon said, "I was not on duty that day, so I conducted inspections in the morning and stayed at my accommodation." (윤 장관은 “(6·3 지방선거일) 퇴근은 몇 시에 했느냐”는 김은혜(경기 성남분당을) 국민의힘 의원 질의에 “저는 그날 근무일이 아니라서 오전에 점검을 하고 숙소에 머물고 있었다”고 했다.)

PPP lawmakers also demanded the resignation of Acting Central Election Commission Chairperson Wi Cheol-hwan that day, but Acting Chairperson Wi refused, saying, "Resigning would be irresponsible." Acting Chairperson Wi was appointed as a standing commissioner of the Central Election Commission by President Lee Jae-myung last year. Within the PPP, there is growing support for impeaching Acting Chairperson Wi if he refuses to resign. The impeachment motion can be proposed solely by the PPP, but for passage in the National Assembly, it requires the approval of a majority of sitting lawmakers, necessitating some support from the Democratic Party. (국민의힘 의원들은 이날도 위철환 중앙선거관리위원장 직무대행의 사퇴를 요구했지만 위 직무대행은 “사퇴는 무책임한 것”이라며 거부했다. 위 직무대행은 지난해 이재명 대통령이 중앙선관위 상임위원으로 임명했다. 국민의힘에서는 위 직무대행이 사퇴를 거부할 경우 탄핵해야 한다는 의견도 커지고 있다. 탄핵안은 국민의힘 단독으로 발의할 수 있지만 국회 통과를 위해선 재적 의원 과반수 찬성이 필요해 민주당 일부가 동조해야 한다.)

The special committee plans to conduct an on-site investigation at the Olympic Park in Songpa-gu, Seoul, and the Songpa-gu Election Commission on the 2nd. During the special committee meeting that day, the issue of whether to deploy police for the on-site investigation at Olympic Park became a point of contention. Democratic Party lawmaker Kim Yong-man (Gyeonggi Hanam-eul) said, "The goal is to enter and conduct inspections alongside individuals from the protesting groups. But how can we possibly enter there without police cooperation?" In response, PPP lawmaker Joo Jin-woo (Busan Haeundae-gap) countered, "If we send an official document to the police requesting that they clear the access routes in advance, who will take responsibility for any physical conflicts that arise?" Previously, some Democratic Party lawmakers had visited Olympic Park but were blocked by protest participants and had to turn back. (국조특위는 2일 서울 송파구 올림픽공원과 송파구선관위에 대한 현장 조사에 나설 예정이다. 이날 국조특위 회의에서는 올림픽공원 현장 조사 때 경찰 투입 여부가 쟁점이 되기도 했다. 민주당 김용만(경기 하남을) 의원은 “시위대 측 인사와 함께 들어가 점검하고 오는 것이 목표인데, 경찰 협조도 없이 어떻게 거기를 들어간단 말이냐”고 했다. 이에 대해 국민의힘 주진우(부산 해운대갑) 의원은 “경찰에 공문을 보내서 진입로를 미리 비워 놓으라고 하면 거기서 나오는 물리적 충돌은 누가 책임지겠느냐”고 했다. 앞서 일부 민주당 의원이 올림픽공원에 갔다가 집회 참가자들에게 막혀 발길을 돌리기도 했다.)

The special committee decided to request assistance in maintaining order from the Seoul Metropolitan Police Agency and the Songpa Police Station. Regarding the rally at Olympic Park, Minister of the Interior and Safety Yoon Ho-Jung stated, "We have not yet reached the stage of making a decision about mobilizing force to disperse them." (국조특위는 일단 서울경찰청과 송파경찰서에 질서 유지 협조를 요청하기로 했다. 윤호중 행안부 장관은 올림픽공원 집회와 관련해 “강제력을 동원해 해산시키는 단계까지는 아직 판단을 못 하는 상황”이라고 했다.)

Meanwhile, in its report to the National Assembly that day, the NEC announced that it would change the printing standard for main ballots from covering more than 50% of voters to 100% of the number of voters, and that adjustments to the ratio would be decided by a vote of the Central Election Commission rather than by the executive authority of the Secretary-General. Noh Tae-ak, former Chairperson of the Central Election Commission, who resigned taking responsibility for the ballot shortage incident, said regarding the fact that he brought his wife on an overseas trip during his tenure as chairperson, "I will either immediately return the (trip expenses) to the state treasury or return them to society through appropriate means." (한편 선관위는 이날 국회 보고에서 본투표 용지 인쇄 기준을 유권자의 50% 이상에서 유권자 수의 100%로 하고, 비율 조정은 사무총장 전결에서 중앙선관위 의결로 하겠다고 밝혔다. 투표용지 부족 사태의 책임을 지고 사퇴한 노태악 전 중앙선관위원장은 위원장 재직 당시 해외 출장에 아내를 동반한 것과 관련해 “(출장 비용을) 바로 국고에 반납하든지 아니면 적절한 방법으로 사회에 환원하겠다”고 했다.)

item.title: This Time, Neutralizing the Filibuster... The Ruling Party's Legislative Dominance Intensifies (이번엔 필리버스터 무력화… 더 거세진 與 입법 독주)
item.description:
This Time, Neutralizing the Filibuster... The Ruling Party's Legislative Dominance Intensifies (이번엔 필리버스터 무력화… 더 거세진 與 입법 독주)

Following the Democratic Party of Korea's forced election of standing committee chairs for the latter half of the 22nd National Assembly, it has now moved to revise the filibuster (unlimited debate) and fast-track (expedited agenda) systems, which were meant to guarantee the minority party's right to speak. With the People Power Party protesting this as "dictatorship backed by a majority of seats," it is interpreted as a clear intent to push through bills desired by the government and ruling party at all costs. According to Democratic Party spokesperson Lee Ju-hee, President Lee Jae-myung had a dinner with the party's leadership on the 1st, urging them to "accelerate the processing of legislative bills related to state tasks in the latter half of the year." <<> Acting Democratic Party leader and floor leader Han Byeong-do stated at the party's supreme council meeting on the same day, "We will strengthen the criteria for requesting and maintaining a filibuster to ensure that even livelihood bills are never again held hostage to political strife." Under current National Assembly law, a filibuster can be terminated 24 hours after it begins with the consent of three-fifths (180 seats) of the registered members. Although the current ruling bloc holds 185 seats, the Democratic Party itself has only 161, meaning it may not be able to end a filibuster without cooperation from parties like the Rebuilding Korea Party (12 seats) on certain issues. Moreover, during the first half of the 22nd National Assembly, when the Democratic Party pushed through contentious bills such as those on prosecutorial reform, the People Power Party responded by filing filibusters even against bills agreed upon by both parties, effectively stalling and blocking their passage. In response, the Democratic Party is now considering pulling out the card of neutralizing the filibuster system itself. <<> Late last year, the Democratic Party had already pushed for an amendment to the National Assembly Act allowing the Assembly Speaker to halt a filibuster if the number of lawmakers present in the plenary session falls below one-fifth (60 seats) of the registered members during the debate. This move is aimed at making it difficult for the People Power Party, which currently holds 110 seats, to maintain a long-term filibuster. However, at the time, criticism arose even from within the ruling bloc, including the Rebuilding Korea Party, that this would undermine a legitimate procedural obstruction tool. That clause was subsequently dropped, but it is now reported that the Democratic Party is considering reintroducing it. <<> Acting leader Han Byeong-do also stated, "We will also revise the hollow fast-track system." Like the filibuster, the threshold for designating a fast-track requires the consent of three-fifths of the registered members, meaning the current ruling bloc can push it through independently. However, bills designated as fast-track are supposed to be processed within 180 days in the standing committee, 90 days in the Legislation and Judiciary Committee, and 60 days for plenary session referral—a total of up to 330 days—and Han said they aim to shorten this time as well. He noted, "The current maximum of 330 days is longer than the average review period for bills passed during the 21st National Assembly," adding, "We will revise the system to enable truly faster bill reviews." <<> The Democratic Party says it will discuss how exactly to reform the fast-track system going forward. In the 22nd National Assembly, Democratic Party lawmaker Jin Seong-jun has already proposed a bill to shorten the review period to 60 days in standing committees and 15 days in the Legislation and Judiciary Committee. Additionally, internal discussions have surfaced about measures such as allowing the replacement of a standing committee chair if they fail to convene meetings or delay bill reviews without just cause. <<> The previous day, the Democratic Party unilaterally elected 11 of the 18 standing committee chairs, including the Legislation and Judiciary Committee, as its own, arbitrarily deciding on them. It stated it would leave the remaining 7 chairs for the People Power Party, but the People Power Party has refused, saying, "We will not accept any standing committee without the normalization of the assembly's organization." The People Power Party argues that it is customary for the second-largest party, not the majority party, to hold the chair of the Legislation and Judiciary Committee. <<> In response, Acting leader Han stated, "I hope the People Power Party will cooperate in electing the remaining 7 standing committee chairs even now. If they kick even this away and obstruct the assembly's operation, we will use every means and method to complete the normalization of the National Assembly." However, People Power Party senior spokesperson Park Seong-hoon called this "an act of violence that tramples on the decades-old parliamentary customs of dialogue and compromise between the ruling and opposition parties, amounting to a death sentence for parliamentarism." The People Power Party is even considering a "total boycott" of the assembly schedule. <<> Amid this, Seo Young-gyo, the Democratic Party lawmaker elected as chair of the Legislation and Judiciary Committee on the 31st, plans to convene a full committee meeting on the 2nd to discuss the appointment of secretaries and the formation of the first subcommittee on bill review. With the People Power Party refusing to participate in any standing committee assignments, including the Legislation and Judiciary Committee, in protest of the unilateral chair elections, this is interpreted as the Democratic Party's intent to push forward with amendments to the Criminal Procedure Act to abolish the prosecution's supplementary investigation rights, among other measures, under its own leadership. (더불어민주당이 22대 국회 후반기 상임위원장 선출을 강행 처리한 데 이어 소수 야당의 발언권 보장을 위한 필리버스터(무제한 토론)와 패스트트랙(신속 처리 안건) 제도까지 손보겠다고 나섰다. 국민의힘이 “다수 의석을 앞세운 독재”라고 반발하는 상황에서 정부·여당이 원하는 법안을 반드시 처리하겠다는 뜻으로 해석됐다. 이재명 대통령은 1일 민주당 원내지도부와 만찬을 하며 “하반기에는 국정과제 관련 입법안 처리에 더욱 속도를 내 줄 것을 당부했다”고 민주당 이주희 원내대변인이 전했다.)

item.title: S. Korea's PM: "High Oil Prices, High Exchange Rates, and Even the Possibility of Rate Hikes—Our Economy Still in Crisis" (韓총리 “고유가·고환율에 금리 인상 가능성까지, 우리 경제 여전히 위기”)
item.description:
Prime Minister Han Sung-sook on the 2nd assessed that "our economy remains in a state of crisis." <<> At an emergency economic review meeting held that morning at the Government Sejong Complex, PM Han stated, "On top of high oil prices and a high exchange rate, the possibility of major countries raising their benchmark interest rates is also growing." <<> Regarding the economic situation in the first half of the year, PM Han evaluated, "Despite the difficulties of the Middle East war, thanks to the government's swift response and the cooperation of the people, we have seen achievements such as stabilizing the supply of petroleum products and daily necessities, increasing exports and investment, and raising the economic growth rate." He added, "As the United States and Iran have signed a memorandum of understanding (MOU) on an armistice and are continuing working-level talks, expectations for stabilization of the Middle East situation are also growing, with international oil prices falling to pre-war levels." <<> Nevertheless, PM Han emphasized that in response to the ongoing crisis, the government must focus on price management and protecting vulnerable groups. <<> PM Han also stated, "In preparation for stabilization of the Middle East situation, we should also prepare measures to strengthen cooperation with the Middle East in advance." He said, "Please restore exports of general machinery and automobiles to the Middle East, actively explore ways our country can contribute to post-war reconstruction efforts, and push forward without disruption the improvement work on the supply chain system of our industries, whose vulnerabilities were exposed by this crisis." <<> PM Han predicted, "It will take considerable time until we overcome this crisis and our economy is fully normalized." However, he added, "If the government meticulously pursues policies with an extraordinary resolve, we can overcome this crisis in a shorter time." (한성숙 국무총리는 2일 “우리 경제가 여전히 위기 상황”이라고 평가했다.)

item.title: [Exclusive] “Dear People Power Party Lawmaker, Would You Like to Play Golf with President Lee?”… Blue House Proposes Surprise Meeting ([단독] “국힘 의원님, 李대통령과 골프 한번 치시죠”… 靑, 깜짝 회동 제안)
item.description:
[Exclusive] “Dear People Power Party Lawmaker, Would You Like to Play Golf with President Lee?”… Blue House Proposes Surprise Meeting ([단독] “국힘 의원님, 李대통령과 골프 한번 치시죠”… 靑, 깜짝 회동 제안)

It was learned on the 1st that President Lee Jae-myung recently proposed golf meetings with multiple senior lawmakers from the People Power Party (PPP) through Blue House officials. A Blue House official reportedly explained, while asking about their attendance, that “President Lee wants to hear the opposition party’s opinions and candid feedback on pending political issues.” (이재명 대통령이 최근 청와대 관계자를 통해 복수의 국민의힘 중진 의원에게 골프 회동을 제안한 것으로 1일 알려졌다. 청와대 관계자는 참석 여부를 물으며 “이 대통령이 정치 현안에 대한 야당의 의견과 쓴소리를 듣고 싶어 한다”고 설명했다고 한다.)

Shin Sung-beom (Sancheong, Hamyang, Geochang, Hapcheon, South Gyeongsang), a three-term PPP lawmaker, received a call from the Blue House on the morning of the 19th of last month. Shin stated, “A senior Blue House official said, ‘President Lee wants to listen to candid feedback by inviting senior opposition lawmakers,’ and proposed a round of golf with President Lee.” Shin added, “I declined because I don’t play golf, but I told the senior Blue House official, ‘It’s a good idea. You should also meet with other opposition lawmakers and hear arguments against the controversy over the cancellation of the indictment.’” (3선인 국민의힘 신성범(경남 산청·함양·거창·합천) 의원은 지난달 19일 오전 청와대에서 전화를 받았다. 신 의원은 “청와대 고위 관계자가 ‘이 대통령이 야당 중진들을 모시고 쓴소리를 들어보려고 한다’며 이 대통령과 함께 골프를 제안했다”고 전했다. 신 의원은 “나는 골프를 치지 않아 거절했지만 청와대 고위 관계자에게 ‘좋은 생각이다. 다른 야당 의원들과 만나 공소 취소 논란에 대해 반대하는 논거도 들어보시라’고 말했다”고 전했다.)

Lawmaker A, a senior figure from the Yeongnam region, reportedly received a proposal for a golf meeting with President Lee from another Blue House official in mid-May. Lawmaker A said, “President Lee initiated the meeting with the intent to properly hear public sentiment, and I see no reason to decline.” He added, “However, since misunderstandings could arise, I replied that I would play golf together when an opportunity arises after the local elections.” According to Lawmaker A, no specific schedule coordination followed the phone call. (영남 중진인 A 의원은 5월 중순 또 다른 청와대 관계자로부터 이 대통령과 골프 회동을 제안받았다고 한다. A 의원은 “이 대통령이 민심을 제대로 듣겠다는 취지로 만남을 청해왔는데 거절할 이유는 없다고 생각한다”며 “다만 괜한 오해가 생길 수 있으니 지방선거 이후에 기회가 되면 같이 골프를 치겠다고 답했다”고 했다. 그러나 전화 통화 이후 구체적인 일정 조율은 없었다는 게 A 의원 설명이다.)

It is not known whether the Blue House proposed golf meetings to other PPP lawmakers. However, the two lawmakers confirmed to have received proposals are both senior figures from the Yeongnam region and are assessed as having weak factional affiliations. (청와대가 다른 국민의힘 의원에게 골프 회동을 제안했는지는 알려지지 않았다. 다만 제안을 받은 것으로 확인된 두 의원은 영남 중진이며, 계파색이 엷다는 평가를 받고 있다.)

In political circles, the Blue House’s proposal for golf meetings is interpreted as part of President Lee’s “expansion of his outreach.” This is seen as being on the same level as President Lee nominating former lawmaker Lee Hye-hoon, a former PPP member, as a candidate for Minister of Planning and Budget (who later stepped down) and holding a private lunch with former Daegu Mayor Hong Joon-pyo. However, a PPP official said, “If President Lee wants to communicate with opposition lawmakers, there are many ways, such as meeting with the opposition leader. I’m not sure what the intention is in selectively proposing golf meetings to some senior lawmakers.” President Lee met with PPP leader Jang Dong-hyuk twice during his first year in office, with the last meeting in April. That meeting was held together with then-Prime Minister Kim Min-seok and several leaders from both the ruling and opposition parties. (정치권에선 청와대의 골프 회동 제안에 대해 이 대통령의 ‘외연 확장’ 행보라는 해석도 나온다. 이 대통령이 국민의힘 출신인 이혜훈 전 의원을 기획예산처 장관 후보자로 지명(이후 낙마)하고, 홍준표 전 대구시장과 비공개 오찬을 하는 것과 같은 차원이라는 것이다. 다만 국민의힘 관계자는 “이 대통령이 야당 의원들과 소통을 원한다면 야당 대표와의 만남 등 여러 방법이 있을 텐데 일부 중진 의원을 골라 골프 회동을 제안한 의도는 무엇인지 모르겠다”고 했다. 이 대통령은 취임 1년간 국민의힘 장동혁 대표를 두 번 만났고, 지난 4월이 마지막이었다. 당시 회동은 김민석 당시 국무총리를 비롯해 여야 지도부 여러 명과 함께 만나는 자리였다.)

After boarding a plane returning to Korea following a European tour on the 17th of last month, President Lee stated on X (formerly Twitter) that U.S. President Donald Trump proposed a round of golf, adding, “I think I need to prepare.” A Blue House official said, “I understand that the President occasionally enjoys sports (golf) with family members and others,” adding, “If the opportunity arises, why couldn’t he play with political figures?” (이 대통령은 지난달 17일 유럽 순방을 마치고 귀국하는 비행기에 오른 후 X(옛 트위터)에서 도널드 트럼프 미 대통령에게 골프를 제안받았다고 밝히면서 “준비를 해야 할 것 같다”고 했다. 청와대 관계자는 “대통령이 종종 가족 등과 운동(골프)을 하는 것으로 안다”며 “기회가 되면 정치권 인사도 함께 칠 수 있지 않겠느냐”고 했다.)

item.title: Opposition: "Baejae High Baseball Team's Suspension Too Severe" (野, 배재고 야구부 징계에 “잘못했지만 6개월 정지는 과도”)
item.description:
Opposition: "Baejae High Baseball Team's Suspension Too Severe" (野, 배재고 야구부 징계에 “잘못했지만 6개월 정지는 과도”)

Key opposition political figures on the 1st criticized the six-month competition suspension imposed on the Baejae High School baseball team, stating, "While the students' actions were wrong, the severity of the punishment is excessive." (야권 주요 정치인들은 1일 배재고 야구부가 6개월 대회 출전 정지 징계를 받은 데 대해 “학생들의 행동은 잘못됐지만 징계 수위가 과도하다”고 지적했다.)

Previously, some student players from the Baejae High baseball team shouted "Let's go to Starbucks" at Gwangju Ilgo players during the 81st Blue Dragon National High School Baseball Championship held at Mokdong Stadium in Seoul on the 29th of last month. This drew criticism for reminiscent of last month's controversy over Starbucks Korea's so-called "May 18 Tank Day" event. (앞서 배재고 야구부 일부 학생 선수들은 지난달 29일 서울 목동구장에서 열린 제81회 청룡기 전국고교야구선수권대회에서 광주일고 선수들을 향해 “스타벅스 가야지”라고 외쳤다. 이는 지난달 스타벅스 코리아의 이른바 ‘5·18 탱크데이’ 이벤트 논란을 연상시킨다는 비판을 받았다.)

People Power Party floor leader Jeong Jeom-sik said on Facebook the same day, "During the game, Baejae High players jeered at Gwangju Ilgo players with a mocking chant of 'Let's go to Starbucks,' which was inappropriate as it demeaned the May 18 Democratization Movement. However, I believe the Korea Baseball Softball Association's six-month suspension of the Baejae High baseball team from national competitions is an excessive measure." (국민의힘 정점식 원내대표는 이날 페이스북에서 “경기 중에 배재고 선수들이 광주일고 선수들에게 ‘스타벅스 가야지’라는 조롱 섞인 구호로 야유한 것은 5·18 민주화운동을 비하한 측면이 있어 부적절한 행동이었다”며 “그러나 대한야구소프트볼협회가 배재고 야구부에 전국대회 출전 6개월 정지 징계를 내린 것은 지나친 조치라고 여겨진다”고 했다.)

Floor leader Jeong added, "For young student-athletes, participating in national competitions is tied to college admissions and their baseball careers. Not all Baejae High players committed the wrongdoing, and many did not join in the taunt, so a six-month suspension for the entire team is excessive." (정 원내대표는 “청소년 운동선수들에게 전국 대회 출전은 대학 진학과 야구 인생이 걸린 일”이라며 “배재고 선수 전체가 잘못을 저지른 것도 아니고, 조롱에 동조하지 않은 선수도 많은데 배재고 야구부 전체에 6개월 출전 정지 징계는 과도하다”고 했다.)

He further stated, "I kindly ask everyone to refrain from excessive punishment or criticism that could crush the dreams of young teenagers who haven't even blossomed in life yet. I earnestly request the Korea Baseball Softball Association to reconsider the suspension measure." (그러면서 “아직 인생의 꽃도 피우지 못한 어린 청소년들의 꿈을 꺾는 과도한 징계나 비난은 자제해 주실 것을 부탁드린다”며 “대한야구소프트볼협회에 출전 정지 조치를 재고할 것을 간곡히 요청드린다”고 했다.)

Independent lawmaker Han Dong-hoon posted on Facebook, "Using the May 18 Gwangju Democratization Movement as material for jeering at an opposing team in a high school baseball game was wrong, but imposing a six-month suspension on young students is excessive." (무소속 한동훈 의원은 페이스북에서 “고교 야구 경기에서 5·18 광주민주화운동을 상대팀에 대한 야유의 소재로 삼은 것은 잘못된 것”이라며 “그러나, 어린 학생들에게 6개월 출전 정지를 하는 것은 과도하다”고 했다.)

Lawmaker Han added, "These are young students. Adult broadcaster Choi Wook, who said on air that they should be 'run over by a tank,' only apologized and continues broadcasting, and Starbucks wasn't shut down either." (한 의원은 “어린 학생들이다. 방송에서 탱크로 밀어버려야 한다고 말한 성인 방송인 최욱씨도 사과만 하고 계속 방송 중이고, 스타벅스도 영업 정지 안 당했다”고 했다.)

Reform Party leader Lee Jun-seok posted on Facebook, "While the actions of some Baejae High students deserve criticism, the six-month competition suspension should be withdrawn." (개혁신당 이준석 대표는 페이스북에서 “배재고 일부 학생의 행동은 비판받아야 마땅하지만 6개월 출전 정지는 철회되어야 한다”고 했다.)

Leader Lee said, "Not long ago, we saw an arrogant Seoul mayoral candidate who beat up seniors, beat up police, beat up citizens trying to intervene, and used May 18 as an excuse. Now, we see a president pushing a person who commemorated the May 18 Eve event at the New Millennium NHK in a passionate way as a party leader." (이 대표는 “얼마 전까지 선배 패고, 경찰 패고, 말리는 시민 패고 5·18 핑계를 대는 오만한 서울시장 후보를 봤다”며 “지금은 대통령이 5·18 전야제를 새천년NHK에서 혈기 넘치는 방법으로 기념한 분을 당 대표로 미는 모습을 보고 있다”고 했다.)

He continued, "It seems those scenes made May 18 seem trivial to the students. If we are overly harsh only to the Baejae High students who grew up seeing those distorted images, that too is unjust." (그러면서 “그런 모습들이 학생들에게 5·18을 가볍게 보이게 만들었나 보다”라며 “그런 일그러진 모습들을 보며 자란 배재고 학생들에게만 필요 이상으로 가혹하다면 그것 또한 정의롭지 못한 것”이라고 했다.)

item.title: Seo Young-kyo's Legislation and Judiciary Committee Convenes Plenary Session on the 2nd... Fast-Track Handling of Contentious Bills (서영교 법사위, 2일 전체회의 소집...쟁점 법안 처리 속도전)
item.description:
Seo Young-kyo's Legislation and Judiciary Committee Convenes Plenary Session on the 2nd... Fast-Track Handling of Contentious Bills (서영교 법사위, 2일 전체회의 소집...쟁점 법안 처리 속도전)

<<>> It was revealed on the 1st that the new chairperson of the Legislation and Judiciary Committee, Seo Young-kyo, has convened a plenary session for the 2nd. This comes just two days after the Democratic Party of Korea unilaterally elected Chairperson Seo as the head of the Legislation and Judiciary Committee during a National Assembly plenary session on the 30th. Amid the People Power Party's consideration of boycotting the National Assembly in response to the ruling party's unilateral selection of standing committee chairs, the committee has begun operating as a "half-formed" entity. <<> According to a compilation of reports from this newspaper on the same day, the Legislation and Judiciary Committee under Seo decided to hold a plenary session at 3 p.m. on the 2nd. The agenda includes the appointment of secretaries and the formation of the First Subcommittee on Bill Review. A source from the People Power Party commented, "The Democratic Party is revealing its intention to unilaterally steer the second half of the National Assembly." <<> The Legislation and Judiciary Committee, led by Seo, is expected to accelerate legislative processes starting with the plenary session on the 2nd. Appearing on YTN Radio that day, Chairperson Seo stated, "As the chair of the Legislation and Judiciary Committee, I must spur reforms based on the seat distribution granted by the people and the historical tasks that must now be carried out." This was interpreted as an intention to speed up the legislation of reform bills for the second half. <<> Immediately, the Democratic Party plans to push forward with amendments to the Criminal Procedure Act and the handling of a special counsel bill regarding manipulated indictments. The Democratic Party holds the position of processing the Criminal Procedure Act amendments before Constitution Day. Given that Chairperson Seo previously served as head of the Special Committee on Parliamentary Inspection for manipulated indictments, it is anticipated that the relevant special counsel bill will also be expedited. <<> The People Power Party has announced a hardline stance, declaring that it will not accept any standing committee without the normalization of the committee formation process. The previous day, after National Assembly Speaker Woo Won-shik forcibly placed lawmakers from his party onto standing committees, all affected People Power Party lawmakers submitted their resignations. <<> The People Power Party is also considering boycotting the entire schedule of the July extraordinary session. A key source within the People Power Party's leadership stated, "We plan to first hold a general meeting of lawmakers on the 2nd to discuss countermeasures and the level of response." ()
